picks.title: Can one photo of your face reveal how ill you are?
picks.excerpt: US researchers report a foundation AI model (FAHR-Face, Lancet Digital Health) that may help doctors judge how ill a patient is from a single photograph of their face.
picks.rationale: A Lancet Digital Health foundation model, FAHR-Face, that estimates how ill a patient is from one face photo, aimed at clinicians' bedside judgement. Nothing like it appears in the 30-day history.

picks.title: 미 소아 자폐 진단 AI 승인
picks.excerpt: 아거스 코그니티브의 18개월~12세 소아 대상 자폐 스펙트럼 장애 진단 AI 소프트웨어가 미국 FDA 승인을 받았다.
picks.rationale: An FDA authorization for Argus Cognitive's AI that diagnoses autism in children aged 18 months to 12 years, so it reaches regulators directly. The full URL (idxno=3013789) and the autism topic are absent from the history.

picks.title: Robotic therapy for stroke patients
picks.excerpt: An adaptive physical rehab system uses generative AI to learn from physical therapists and offer personalized support to stroke patients.
picks.rationale: An adaptive robotic rehab system that learns from physical therapists to deliver personalized stroke rehabilitation, an AI tool used with patients. It is a different disease and modality from the 10-08 Parkinson's telerehab trial.

picks.title: Expertise modulates automation bias and sentinel behavior in human-AI collaborative diagnosis of neonatal pneumoperitoneum
picks.excerpt: Tests the assumption that AI sensitivity plus clinician oversight adds up: in neonatal pneumoperitoneum diagnosis, clinician expertise shaped automation bias and whether readers caught AI errors.
picks.rationale: Finds that clinician expertise determines whether readers catch AI errors or defer to them in neonatal pneumoperitoneum diagnosis, which bears on how human oversight of diagnostic AI is designed. It asks a different question from the 10-14 neonatal continual-learning study.

picks.title: Why teaching AI about symmetry could make prenatal diagnosis more reliable
picks.excerpt: A new AI model called E(3)-Pose helps capture high-resolution images of a fetus's head to improve early detection of developmental anomalies during pregnancy.
picks.rationale: E(3)-Pose, a symmetry-aware model that steers high-resolution fetal head imaging toward earlier detection of developmental anomalies in prenatal care. No prenatal or fetal-imaging story appears in the history, and the pick adds a fifth outlet.
